newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile trade deficit caused by copper export fall.
newsitem.headline: Chile trade deficit caused by copper export fall.

text.p: A sharp fall in copper exports was the main factor behind August's trade deficit which swung Chile's trade figures from a surplus in the seven months to July to a $30 million deficit for the year through August, said the Central Bank.
Chile, the world's largest copper producer, reported a trade surplus of $236.4 million from January to July and a $1.4 billion surplus in the first eight months of last year.
Bank figures showed a trade deficit of $267 million last month compared with a $76 million deficit a year ago.

A slowdown in import growth in August failed to make up for the drop in copper exports -- which account for 40 percent of Chile's export income -- and a fall in other main exports, said the Bank in its fortnightly report.

"Despite the slight fall in imports registered compared with the same month 1995, the fall in the total value of exports as the result of the sharp decline in copper exports togther with falls in other main exports caused August's deficit," it said.
Bank figures showed exports totalled $1.17 billion last month, down 15 percent from August last year.
Non-traditional exports, which range from wine to salmon to computer software, rose three percent in August against the same period last year.
Imports dipped a scant one percent to $1.44 billion mainly as the result of a four percent fall in imports of intermediate and capital goods.
Imports of consumer goods remained high, rising nine percent last month compared with the same period in 1995.
